# Base image with Flux, OpenMPI, and EFA support for ARM on AWS
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, including git, cmake, and essential certificates.
# Clean up apt cache to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    make \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set environment variables to use the MPI compiler wrappers provided by the base image.
# This ensures that Kripke is compiled with MPI support.
ENV CC=mpicc
ENV CXX=mpicxx

# Define the source directory for clarity
ARG APP_SRC_DIR=/opt/kripke

# Clone the Kripke repository, build it from source, install the executable, and clean up.
# --recurse-submodules is required to fetch the BLT build system dependency.
# Kripke is configured with MPI enabled for multi-node execution.
# FIX: The build process generates 'kripke.exe', so the install command is updated
# to copy 'bin/kripke.exe' to '/usr/local/bin/kripke' for PATH compatibility.
# The source code and build directories are removed to create a lean final image.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recurse-submodules --branch master https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git ${APP_SRC_DIR} \
    && cd ${APP_SRC_DIR} \
    && mkdir build \
    && cd build \
    && cmake .. \
    -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && install -m 755 bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke \
    && cd / \
    && rm -rf ${APP_SRC_DIR}

# Set the default command to show kripke help message
CMD ["kripke", "--help"]

# MiniCluster manifest to run Kripke on a single AWS ARM-based CPU node,
# configured to run across nodes and utilize AWS EFA for networking.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster job.
  name: kripke-aws-arm
  # Deploying to the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The initial number of pods (nodes) to start for the job.
  size: 1

  # The maximum number of pods the MiniCluster can scale up to.
  maxSize: 4

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run. This will start with 1 task on 1 pod.
  tasks: 1

  # Ensure the job resources are not deleted after completion to allow for log/data inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Settings for the Flux Operator's logging verbosity.
  logging:
    # Fail on any error, ensuring robust error handling.
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for the flux view container, required for ARM instances.
    arch: "arm"
    container:
      # As instructed, the flux binaries are expected to be in the main application container.
      disable: true
      # ARM-specific image for flux tools, used if disable were false.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy

  # Defines the main application container. Only one container is permitted.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to be executed by flux. 'flux run' is prepended by the operator.
      command: kripke
      # The main application container MUST NOT be the launcher.
      launcher: false
      # Always pull the latest version of the container image for consistency.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      # Resource requests and limits for AWS Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA).
      # This is required for high-performance networking on supported AWS instances.
      resources:
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1

# Corrected MiniCluster manifest for Kripke based on failure analysis.
# The previous attempt failed due to memory exhaustion on the worker nodes.
# This version scales the job to 4 nodes and 256 tasks to distribute the
# memory load more effectively across a larger number of MPI ranks.
# The problem size (--zones) is also adjusted to balance per-rank memory
# usage while pursuing a larger, more performant problem.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name remains the same for this job configuration.
  name: kripke-aws-arm
  # Deploying to the default namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Scaling up to 4 nodes to increase aggregate memory and distribute the workload.
  size: 4
  # The maximum size is maintained at 4 nodes.
  maxSize: 4
  # Increased task count to 256 to reduce memory pressure on each individual rank.
  tasks: 256

  # Ensure the job resources are not deleted after completion for debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Settings for the Flux Operator's logging verbosity.
  logging:
    # Fail on any error, ensuring robust error handling.
    strict: true

  # Pod-specific configurations.
  pod:
    # The nodeSelector ensures pods are scheduled on specific AWS instance types.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge

  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for the flux view container, required for ARM instances.
    arch: arm
    container:
      # The flux binaries are expected to be in the main application container.
      disable: true
      # ARM-specific image for flux tools.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy

  # Defines the main application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command updated with a new process grid and problem size suitable for 256 ranks.
      command: kripke --procs 8 8 4 --zones 108,108,108 --niter 10 --dset 8
      # The main application container MUST NOT be the launcher.

      # Always pull the latest version of the container image for consistency.
